decisions.statement: The manifests come from the code the page names and from nowhere else.
Code emitting no manifest for the workload its page names is refused.
A manifest with a value nothing filled in is refused before anything is applied.
The namespace is applied first and the workload last.
An apply takes whatever field ownership the apply needs.
A manifest is written beside the code that emitted the manifest before the manifest is applied.
Whether a manifest already exists is asked of the cluster rather than remembered.
A workload with a pod template is waited on until its rollout is done.
A kubectl that refuses stops the apply where the apply is.
What comes between is put up after the namespace is opened and before the rest is applied.
A run that comes between and refuses stops the apply.
A put up handed nothing to come between applies every manifest.
Nothing here builds the app a pod serves.
Asking whether a manifest already matches reaches the namespace the apply reaches.
A plan may name no workload, so what is applied is the manifests alone.
Manifests planned under no workload keep the order the code emitted them in.
A plan naming no workload is placed by each manifest's own body.
A plan naming no workload is waited on by no rollout.

definition: the manifests a cluster service's code emits, put into the cluster
